title: Ben Johnson on Week 5 loss | Press Conference
headline: Bears QB Caleb Williams is 'on track' but his return timing is uncertain, and Tyson Bagent was pulled after two interceptions in favor of Case Keenum.
summary: Ben Johnson said the Bears did not show up against Green Bay: they committed five turnovers on offense, failed to execute in the run or pass game, and allowed four completions of 40+ yards on defense. He credited the Packers' aggressive plan and said Chicago had chances to get back into the game but didn't capitalize. Johnson took responsibility for the offensive play-calling and preparation, and praised Jonathan Gannon's defensive game plan. He said the QB change to Case Keenum came after Tyson Bagent's second interception, as a spark attempt, and that he had not yet diagnosed Bagent's interceptions. On Caleb Williams, Johnson said he is on track after returning to practice, and it will be close whether he plays against Atlanta or after. He had not yet received feedback from Williams' Sunday field workout. Johnson said the staff will decide the Week 6 starter after reviewing this game, and that the process won't change. Johnson also said the offense could stretch the field more going forward.

injuries.detail: Listed among three injuries of note with a hamstring issue (transcript says 'Tyreke'); no timeline given.
Quad injury; Johnson said the team will see what it looks like Monday.
Returned to practice Friday and worked out on the field Sunday; Johnson said he is on track, with a return possible against Atlanta or the week after.

topics.detail: Johnson said the defense let too many balls over the top, allowing four 40-plus-yard passes, and that Green Bay's defense was fast and well-coached, with safeties and linebackers making real-time adjustments.
The offense committed five turnovers, including three interceptions, and struggled in both the run and pass game. Johnson said he would look at his own play-calling and preparation first.

title: Zac Taylor Recaps Win over Miami | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Tee Higgins played through a questionable tag, Ja'Marr Chase cleared protocol, and Joe Burrow's thumb jam is minor; the Bengals now get a bye before at Baltimore.
summary: Taylor credited Miami for fighting to the end and praised Jeff Hafley's work with the Dolphins. He listed the Bengals' issues: two personal fouls, two red-zone fumbles, a kickoff caught on the four, a field-goal penalty that led to a touchdown, and over 200 rushing yards allowed. He said the bye arrives at a good time after three straight close games, and the team will regroup at 3-2 before Baltimore in two weeks. He said the defense's late turnover made the final margin feel safer. On the run game, he said the ground success was mostly how the game unfolded, with Miami playing underneath and in shells, and he called the team's backs a strength he trusts. He downplayed Burrow's hand injury as a jammed thumb on his non-throwing hand. He said Tee Higgins had wanted to play and showed it in practice, and that Ja'Marr Chase had cleared concussion protocol on Saturday. He praised Tanner Hudson as dependable and versatile, able to play multiple spots, and said he needed the defense to settle on its nickel and base personnel. He called the heat historically extreme and said the players fought through exhaustion.

title: DeMeco Ryans on First Win, Will Anderson Jr. & C.J. Stroud | Full Q&A
headline: Texans earn first win; Stroud and Will Anderson praised, while David Montgomery is dealing with a groin injury and a shoulder issue under evaluation.
summary: Ryans said the first win was a relief and credited faith and persistence through a difficult start to the season. He called it a complementary performance with all three phases working together, though the second half was where the team had struggled. He said the offense controlled the game, with stalls in the red zone from self-inflicted penalties leading to field goals. He praised C.J. Stroud for making plays when needed, including a rushing touchdown, and said Stroud's command and comfort in year two are showing. The defense forced turnovers and generated pressure, and Ryans highlighted Will Anderson's three-sack game and his ability to move between edge and interior spots. He said Azeez Al-Shaair is back in the lineup and is the defense's field general, and he gave Reed Blankenship credit for growing comfortable in coverage. On injuries, Ryans said Tank Dell is practicing again and the team hopes he returns to game action, while David Montgomery has a groin injury that may cost him time and a shoulder injury still being evaluated.

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Broncos
headline: Harbaugh owns the failed fourth-and-1 go at the Denver 41 that swung momentum; Herbert's turnover streak was defended as a situational problem, and the team is 0-5 with Kansas City next.
summary: Harbaugh took full responsibility for going for it on fourth-and-1 from the 41, calling it the wrong decision and saying he has never been more upset with himself. He said the players played hard on offense, defense, and special teams, and that the failed call turned momentum even though the team had a seven-point lead. Asked about the offense, he said the direction is improving, pointing to the young offensive linemen, the drives and touchdowns, and the effort of the running backs. He defended quarterback Justin Herbert, saying the late turnovers came from being put in fourth-and-6 situations where he had to take chances, and he took accountability for that. On the 0-5 start, he said he didn't have a clear message beyond players fighting. When asked about the offensive linemen missing from the lineup, including Rashawn Slater, he said he didn't know when they would return for Kansas City. He framed the path forward as staying the course and making sound critical decisions.

injuries.detail: Reporter said he is among the missing linemen; Harbaugh did not address his status and said he didn't know if the linemen would be back for Kansas City.

signals.claim: Late turnovers came from being put in fourth-and-6 situations where he had to force plays, not from his own decisions.
signals.note: Five straight games with a turnover is a concern for fantasy, but Harbaugh blamed game situations, so the QB's usage and risk profile should be watched.
signals.quote: Trying to trying to make a play.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said going for fourth-and-1 at the Denver 41 was the wrong call, that he should have called timeout and punted after seeing the defensive alignment, and that he takes full blame.
Harbaugh praised the defense for multiple stops, three-and-outs, and a big turnover, and said it played its heart out.
The team started a rookie offensive lineman, and Harbaugh praised the young linemen for their play, though he did not name them.
Harbaugh said he had no clear message for a 0-5 team beyond players fighting hard, and that the plan is to keep working harder and smarter.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 11, 2026
headline: Sirianni took full blame for the end-of-game decision in the 19-17 London loss to Jacksonville; no concrete player or injury news for fantasy purposes.
summary: Sirianni took full responsibility for the final-minute decision that cost Philadelphia the 19-17 loss to Jacksonville in London, saying he did not make the right call and that the players fought hard. He declined to explain his thought process in detail, saying only that he had not done his job well enough in that situation. He acknowledged the clock-management options, including taking a knee or running the ball to set up a field goal, and said the loss of yards was a factor in the decision. He called the situation gray, said he had watched many similar late-game situations around the league, and said he would stand by owning the mistake. He praised the defense for keeping the team in the game and said the offense had struggled in the second half despite good first-half production. On the Jacksonville kickoff return, he said he would review the play and noted that the team had put extra players at safety on kickoffs. Asked whether injuries affected personnel on that play, he said no and expressed total faith in the players on the field. He framed accountability as a core program value and described the London atmosphere as strong, with the crowd largely on Philadelphia's side.

topics.detail: Sirianni repeatedly owned the late-game decision and declined to detail his reasoning, saying he would stand by full accountability.
He praised the defense for keeping the team in the game, but said the offense needs to fix its second-half production, which he attributed to scheme and execution.
Sirianni said he would review the kickoff play and noted the team uses extra safeties on kickoffs; he denied injuries affected the personnel on the field.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/11/26
headline: Quinn takes full blame for the end-of-game clock decision in a tie, while Jayden Daniels returned from missed time and played sharply.
summary: Quinn called the game a hard-fought tie that felt like a loss. He said the late-game decision to run for more yards instead of clocking the ball or throwing it out was his responsibility, not Daniels'. He said the team had the chance to win in all three phases and did not seize it, and he praised Daniels' overtime forced fumble on defense. On Daniels, Quinn said it was great to have him back, and he highlighted his line-of-scrimmage reads against blitzes, his willingness to use his legs without forcing it, and his accurate throws to Terry McLaurin and Treylon Burks in crunch time. On defense, Quinn said the unit needs to close out games and shut the door when leading, and that the team is digging in on its response after second-half collapses. He said the penalties, especially pre-snap ones, are being addressed but that he has not yet reviewed the Amik Robertson pass interference call at the goal line. He acknowledged injuries in the secondary and at receiver, and said the team handled the depth challenge well. He said the team will rebound, and that the end-of-game situation will be drilled more heavily in practice.

injuries.detail: Returned after missing time and played the full game, which Quinn called sharp.
Quinn said the team dealt with injuries in the secondary and at receiver and had to ready multiple players late in the week, but did not name them.

signals.claim: Will keep using his legs when needed, without forcing runs, and manage the offense sharply
signals.note: Quinn's praise for his legs and decision-making suggests a stable dual-threat role, which supports rushing upside.

signals.claim: Was a key target for Daniels in crunch-time moments
signals.note: Quinn singled him out for accurate late-game delivery, reinforcing his place in the high-leverage passing game.
signals.quote: you look at Terry, deliver the ball in the right location

signals.claim: Was targeted in crunch-time situations, with Daniels delivering the ball in the right location
signals.note: Mentioned alongside McLaurin as a late-game option, but the mention was brief, so his role remains uncertain.

topics.detail: Quinn said the team should have clocked the ball early instead of trying to gain more yards for a kick, and that he has no timeouts-related excuses. He said the situation will be drilled more in walkthroughs, practices, and two-minute work.

Quinn said the defense allowed three straight touchdown drives after holding the opponent to about six points through most of the third quarter. He said the team has been digging in on its response and needs to close out games with a lead.
Quinn said he wants pre-snap penalties corrected and has not yet formed an assessment. He had not yet reviewed the Amik Robertson goal-line pass interference call.
